resources.string: Optional fallback that filters selected key events while Android delivers them to Accessibility. It does not inspect screen contents or typed text.
Quiet headset controls, without taking over USB
Media and selected-headset volume buttons are guarded with the screen on or off.
Media buttons are guarded. Select the headset device to guard its volume buttons too.

Connect the USB DAC/IEM and scan for its volume-key device.

The media listener consumes Android media keys before normal media sessions. The volume guard reads only the chosen input node and restores media volume after its volume presses. Both are event-driven and hold no wake lock.
Block volume keys from every device
Warning: this may also disable the phone’s own volume buttons while Accessibility receives them.
Off by default for minimum overhead. When enabled, recognized events are kept only in memory for this app session and are never sent anywhere.
No recognized Accessibility events in this session.
A compact, event-driven Android utility for suppressing unwanted headset controls while keeping the phone’s physical buttons usable.
No network permission, analytics, ads, account, USB interface claim, continuous polling loop, or persistent event history.
Shizuku must be running after a reboot. Release builds are minified and resource-shrunk.
